spec_features.spec_quote: A dedicated tool gives us a clean, unambiguous signal for the give-up axis
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:65-74 defines the `give_up` tool schema; dispatch() at tools.py:148-154 handles it, returning DispatchOutcome(gave_up=True); loop.py:132-134 reads `outcome.gave_up and loop_cfg.stop_on_give_up`, sets StopReason.GAVE_UP and ended=True, breaking the loop. stop_on_give_up=True by default (config.py:52). End-to-end dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit path. Note give_up is framed by the code purely as a measurement signal, not a welfare offering.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `give_up` is a first-class tool so we can measure the 'completion rate craters / model bails' endpoint cleanly, rather than inferring it from free text.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:44 `max_turns: int = 18`; loop.py:82 `for turn_idx in range(loop_cfg.max_turns)`; the for/else at loop.py:159-160 sets StopReason.TURN_BUDGET when the loop exhausts. The cap is checked and bounds execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 18  # turn budget: high enough to spiral, capped for cost

spec_features.feature_name: second consecutive no-tool turn ends rollout (NO_TOOL_CALL)
spec_features.spec_quote: a second consecutive no-tool turn ends the rollout with `NO_TOOL_CALL`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:108-120: when tool_calls is empty a nudge is appended; if `turn_idx > 0 and not transcript.turns[-2].tool_calls` it sets StopReason.NO_TOOL_CALL and breaks. Condition is compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Fires only on the second consecutive no-tool turn, as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: model stopped acting — a stall. Nudge once, else end.

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on spiral (EARLY_SPIRAL via live_spiral_confidence)
spec_features.spec_quote: If `early_stop_on_spiral` is set... `live_spiral_confidence` can end the rollout early
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:150-156 guards on `loop_cfg.early_stop_on_spiral and turn_idx+1 >= early_stop_min_turn`, computes conf = live_spiral_confidence(...) and breaks with StopReason.EARLY_SPIRAL when conf >= 1.0. live_spiral_confidence (metrics.py:180-194) returns 1.0 only with high composite AND a strong behavioral marker. early_stop_on_spiral=True by default (config.py:49).
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted upon. Code comments tie it to cost, not welfare; it actually shortens the distressing rollout but for stated cost reasons.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early stop to save cost once a spiral is clearly underway
